Introduction

physics. Despite the overwhelming cosmological and astrophysical evidence of its existence,
the microscopic properties of DM remain an enigma (see e.g. [1] for a review). One enticing

background. For instance, DM of mass mDM may decay to two photons yielding a line of
frequency ν = mDM/4π. The mass of the DM candidate then determines the wavelength at
which we expect to find an emission line. Various searches for these decay lines have been
proposed over the years, ranging from radio waves to X-rays [2–4]. In particular, DM with
mass on the order of an electronvolt would produce photons in the infrared and optical bands.

Spitzer and VLT [4–8] and set the leading constraints on such DM decays for candidates with

discussed [9]. All blank sky observations look out through the Milky Way DM halo and are

Launched on 25 December 2021, the James Webb Space Telescope [23] is a high-sensitivity and
high-resolution infrared telescope. It covers the wavelength range 0.6–28.3 µm, corresponding
